    <a href="economics/public-choice-theory.html" class="framework-card">

      <p class="card-summary">Application of microeconomic models to political decision-making, rejecting the assumption of benevolent bureaucrats.</p>
    </a>

    <a href="society/tragedy-of-the-commons.html" class="framework-card">
      <span class="card-category-badge badge-society">Society</span>
      <h3 class="card-title">Tragedy of the Commons</h3>
      <p class="card-summary">Individual rational exploitation leading to systematic exhaustion of open-access, finite shared resources.</p>
    </a>

    <a href="society/ostrom-polycentric-governance.html" class="framework-card">
      <span class="card-category-badge badge-society">Society</span>

      <p class="card-summary">Complex community institutions successfully governing shared commons without central command or privatization.</p>
    </a>

    <a href="policy/regulatory-capture.html" class="framework-card">
      <span class="card-category-badge badge-policy">Policy</span>
      <h3 class="card-title">Regulatory Capture</h3>
      <p class="card-summary">Government regulatory agencies coming under the dominance of the commercial interests they were designed to regulate.</p>
    </a>

    <a href="policy/goodharts-law.html" class="framework-card">
      <span class="card-category-badge badge-policy">Policy</span>
      <h3 class="card-title">Goodhart's Law</h3>
      <p class="card-summary">When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure as actors game the metric.</p>
    </a>

    <a href="law/subsidiarity.html" class="framework-card">
      <span class="card-category-badge badge-law">Law</span>
      <h3 class="card-title">Subsidiarity</h3>

    </a>
